actions.name: Spend from a Bitcoin P2WSH multisig
actions.summary: k of an account's n keys spend its coins. The address commits to the keys and k, so a member's disclosure is checked by re-deriving it, with no chain read. Members sign in-app through the keystore, or a signer outside muster signs an exported PSBT; any member settles through their own Bitcoin node.

fields.name: inputs
fields.means: the coins spent: txid, vout, value (sat), scriptPubKey, sequence — every prevout carried so every signer can re-derive the hashes and the fee

fields.name: outputs
fields.means: the payee first, then change back to the account (unless dust): value + address or scriptPubKey

fields.name: fee
fields.means: the declared fee in sat; must equal inputs − outputs

steps.who: the proposer (a member; any member may propose)
steps.does: Chooses the account ('btc-p2wsh@<CAIP-10>', coordinate_set_policy) and calls coordinate_propose_btc_spend(pay_to, amount_sat, fee_rate). The module needs Settings → btc-rpc (the user's own Bitcoin Core node): it reads the account's coins with scantxoutset, keeps only coins whose scriptPubKey is the account's, and builds the spend largest coin first until the payment and its fee are covered — payee first, change back to the account unless it would be dust (then it goes to the fee). The fee is fee_rate × an upper bound of the signed vsize and is declared as inputs − outputs. Every input carries its prevout (amount + scriptPubKey). The driver's gate runs before anything is published; then the policy, the effect, and the context are published (environment = the chain's CAIP-2 bip122:<genesis>, account = the account's address, slot = the intent id, expiry), and the coin read is recorded in the log as an external read (source 'bitcoind:scantxoutset'), so every signer can account for the inputs (invariant 10). The materialization every member re-derives: dCBOR ['bip143.p2wsh.sortedmulti.v1', <CAIP-2 chain>, [each input's BIP-143 sighash]].

steps.who: each member whose key is one of the account's (in muster)
steps.does: coordinate_readiness first: the Bitcoin RPC is infrastructure this proposal introduces (missing until configured); the chain is graded by asking THAT node which chain it serves; the authority is whether MY key is one of the account's — never who else holds one. Approve signs in-app: the driver's hook has the keystore sign every input with the member's secp256k1 key and attest over P with the same key, so the approval is 'committed'. A key that is not the account's makes a contribution the driver rejects: nothing published.
steps.signs: per input, the BIP-143 sighash: nVersion, hashPrevouts, hashSequence, this input's outpoint, scriptCode = the witnessScript (OP_k <the n keys, sorted> OP_n OP_CHECKMULTISIG), THIS input's amount, nSequence, hashOutputs, nLocktime, SIGHASH_ALL — signed ECDSA, DER, low-S (RFC 6979) by the member's keystore key. The contribution is dCBOR {signer: the 33-byte key, sigs: [one DER signature per input]}; the attestation is a recoverable secp256k1 signature by the same key over P

steps.who: a signer outside muster (seam S8) — a hardware signer, Sparrow, Bitcoin Core
steps.does: Any member clicks 'Sign outside muster (PSBT)': coordinate_export_outside gives the proposal's spend as a base64 PSBT — each input's witness UTXO and witnessScript; the signer's partial signatures (SIGHASH_ALL) come back. Nothing is signed or published by the export. The outside signer signs and hands the PSBT back; Import (coordinate_import_outside) has the DRIVER read it: every account key that signed EVERY input becomes a contribution, verified like a native one, and is published as a pasted approval. It counts toward k and every member sees it graded 'unattested' (signed outside muster), never 'committed'.
steps.signs: the outside signer signs the same per-input hashes in its own device; muster signs nothing here

reveals.field: the PSBT (the unsigned spend + prevouts + scripts)

steps.who: any member, through their own Bitcoin node
steps.does: coordinate_submit once the fold says executable (Settings → btc-rpc required: 'no-bitcoin-node' otherwise). The Bitcoin settlement re-runs the driver's gate, re-derives every input's sighash, admits only contributions the driver names a key for — one per key — refuses below k, and finalizes the witness per input: an empty CHECKMULTISIG dummy, exactly k signatures (+ the SIGHASH_ALL byte) in the witnessScript's sorted-key order, then the witnessScript. The broadcast transaction's non-witness bytes ARE the reviewed spend and its txid is the one the payload names; the node relays it (sendrawtransaction). The settlement holds no key; no one signs anything new.
steps.signs: nothing new — the collected signatures become the witnesses

reveals.field: policy (the witnessScript / executed leaf: k and all n keys)

steps.who: no one — the node is read
steps.does: Finality is read from the node (getrawtransaction): final at 1 confirmation on regtest, 6 elsewhere — observed, never asserted. On a final read the room publishes a final event.

refusals.what: a spend with an input that is not this account's coins
refusals.why: signRefusal: 'input <i> spends coins that are not this account's' — before anyone is asked to sign

refusals.what: a declared fee that is not exactly inputs − outputs
refusals.why: BIP-143 signs only each input's own amount, so a wrong prevout would silently change the fee; the declared fee must equal inputs − outputs, and every signer re-derives it from the carried prevouts

refusals.what: an output below the dust limit (546 sat)
refusals.why: signRefusal refuses a dust output before anyone signs; the builder never makes dust change — it goes to the fee

refusals.what: a spend the account's coins cannot pay
refusals.why: the builder raises ('not enough in the account') — never a spend that could not be broadcast

refusals.what: a signature by a key that is not one of the account's
refusals.why: the driver verifies each input's signature for an account key only; the live path answers 'rejected' and publishes nothing

refusals.what: a signature over another spend's hashes
refusals.why: invariant 1: every member re-derives each input's sighash from the logged effect; a signature over any other bytes does not verify, and settlement drops it

refusals.what: a key_ref other than the key the Bitcoin hook signs with
importing an outside signer's PSBT of a different spend
refusals.why: 'not-this-spend': the PSBT's canonical form (unsigned tx + each input's prevout + spending script) must equal the proposal's; nothing is published

refusals.what: a PSBT that carries no account signature, or is not a PSBT

refusals.why: 'insufficient-signatures', naming have and need; a stranger's, another spend's, or a repeated signature never counts

refusals.what: a disclosure whose address does not commit to its keys and k
refusals.why: the address is re-derived from the disclosed keys and k; a mismatch is refused, never trusted

refusals.what: taking part without a Bitcoin node configured
refusals.why: readiness grades the node as missing (with a remedy) and the chain as unknown, never met; the hosted propose and submit answer 'no-bitcoin-node' — a spend is read and settled only through the user's own node

refusals.what: an in-app approval when the recorded coin read is missing from the log
refusals.why: invariant 10: the spend declares its inputs as an external read; the generic 'unaccountable-input' refusal is proven on the live path for the safe and threshold policies

refusals.what: a contribution published under a name that is not its signer's
refusals.why: it is nobody's approval: the fold and every view drop it before dedup, so one signer never counts twice and a forgery never takes a member's slot (exo-a5a)

actions.ui: The account first: Room → Accounts → Bitcoin multisig (P2WSH or Taproot, k, network, each member's key from Settings → YOUR BITCOIN KEY) → Disclose. Then Room → + → Payment → Settles via Bitcoin (P2WSH) → From <account> → payee + amount (sat) + fee (sat/vB) → Propose; card → Approve, or 'Sign outside muster (PSBT)' → Copy PSBT / Import. Settle on-chain in the ready box (coordinate_submit) — shown because the family's profile settles on a chain.

claims.claim: The chain itself checks k of n: nothing — no module, no guard, no admin — gets around the script
A signature spends only these exact coins: it is bound through the outpoints, not a chain id

The fee is implicit in what each signer signs (BIP-143 commits to its own input's amount); muster makes it explicit — every prevout is carried and the declared fee must equal inputs − outputs before anyone signs
Muster signs only what it re-derived; an outside signer's signature counts only if the driver verifies it, and it is always shown as signed outside muster
At spend the chain learns the policy (k and all n keys) and which k signed — P2WSH and a single-leaf tapscript reveal the same
The user's node learns the account's address when the proposer reads its coins, and sees the signed spend before the network
A collected signature never expires; revoking means double-spending an input

evidence.what: BIP-143: the segwit v0 sighash — commits to this input's amount only

unverified: The card's amount → payee line for a Bitcoin spend comes from the module's effect summary (the payment outputs, change excluded; card_words_test); it has not been seen on screen.

coordinate_submit polls the node for about four seconds; if the spend is not final by then it returns pending, and nothing later publishes the final event for a Bitcoin intent (only LEZ settles are re-watched by the pump). From reading nim-lib/muster_module.nim, not a test.
